summary: The checked-out implementation allowed asyncio.CancelledError raised inside Request.is_disconnected() to escape from both request-state polling branches. A narrow wrapper now treats receive-only cancellation as a client disconnect, while propagating cancellation when the surrounding handler task is itself being cancelled. Both branches abort the affected scheduler request through their existing paths.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact request.is_disconnected() CancelledError injection: waiting and running request branches failed by propagating CancelledError; genuine handler-task cancellation boundary passed. Raw output: evidence/unit-before.log.
Four focused cases passed: waiting-request abort, running-request abort, ordinary connected result preservation, and propagation of genuine task cancellation. Raw output: evidence/unit-after.log.
The complete tokenizer-manager request-state cleanup module passed: 30 tests and 3 subtests. Raw output: evidence/unit-full-after.log.
A real single-gfx950 SGLang server survived an abrupt TCP close, returned HTTP 200 from /health, and served a subsequent four-token GPU generation. Raw server log and probe.json are retained.

gpu_execution.evidence: Single AMD gfx950 GPU; the tiny deterministic Llama server loaded with the Triton attention backend and produced follow-up output_ids [104, 40, 16, 93] after the disconnect. See evidence/gpu-disconnect/probe.json and server.log.

remaining_limitations: The reported 4x NVIDIA RTX 6000D (SM120), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash weights, ~200,000-token prompt, TP=4 topology, and original container image were unavailable, so that full deployment was not reproduced.

The qualified tiny random Llama fixture validates HTTP transport and real engine execution only; it does not validate DeepSeek architecture behavior, semantic accuracy, long-context behavior, or distributed execution.

The real HTTP probe exercised an abrupt TCP disconnect and engine survival, while the deterministic unit regression supplied the issue-specific CancelledError at the exact tokenizer-manager polling call sites.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The prepared interpreter does not contain the ruff module; pytest and git diff --check were used for validation.
